newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison confident on Hong Kong in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison confident on Hong Kong in 1997.

text.p: Hutchison Whampoa Ltd said it expects to see further economic recovery in Hong Kong in 1997 and remains confident about the territory's future.
"The Group has complete confidence in Hong Kong," chairman Li Ka-shing told shareholders shortly after reporting a 25.6-percent increase in net profit to HK$12.02 billion ($1.55 billion) in 1996.

"During 1996 we witnessed a gradual recovery in Hong Kong's economy with rallies in both the stock market and property sectors. This recovery is likely to be further enhanced in the months ahead with expected increases in China's exports and imports," Li said.

Hutchison Whampoa's overall strategy is to continue to expand its core business in Hong Kong, China and elsewhere, particularly in Asia, and to boost its recurrent income base while maximising coordination among its businesses, Li said.

Rental income is showing steady growth and property construction work is on schedule, he said. Declining profits from completed property developments were offset in 1996 by increases in investment income.
A replenished land bank and projects in China "provide the potential for future growth in profitability," Li said.
Throughput growth at container terminal operations in Kwai Chung slowed in line with the downturn in Hong Kong's export performance but operational efficiency improved, Li said.

Hutchison's Hongkong International Terminals Ltd was awarded rights to develop, commission and operate two berths at Terminal 9 on Tsing Yi Island while a 33-percent owned subsidiary acquired the right to develop a site in Tuen Mun into a new river trade container handling facility.
Steps have also been taken to enhance container terminal operations and profitability and expand international container terminal operations, Li said.
A.S. Watson & Company made solid progress through improved efficiencies and cost controls, recording a strong increase in profits, Li said.

In Hutchison's telecommunications operations, the virtual completion of the changeover from two limited capacity analogue systems into two digital systems substantially increased cellular phone subscriber capacity, which was increased further with the awarding of a Personal Communications Services licence.
Li said Hutchison's cellular telephone subscriber base now stands at about 340,000.
"(It) has tripled since the end of 1995 and the prospects for growth are encouraging," Li said.

Orange Plc more than doubled its subscriber base to 888,000, acquiring an 11-percent share of the overall U.K. network. The flotation of Orange was completed in April, at which time the Group's effective interest declined to 48.22 percent. It has subsequently been increased to 49.02 percent.

Husky Oil performed well during the year, and obtained an investment grade rating through two international rating agencies, Li said. The company subsequently refinanced its debt on a stand-alone basis.
